Hi Team (Atlas procurement + AWS marketplace),

Thanks again for the time yesterday — excited about the opportunity to make Redwood available via an AWS private offer tailored to AtlasHealth's compliance needs and consumption profile. I pulled together two packaging options so we can converge quickly: a) Reserved capacity (committed monthly node-hours) + metered overage, or b) Pure metered private offer with list-price anchoring and short-term credits.

Quick asks so we can finalize the private offer template:
- For channel/reseller routing: do you require the partner (if any) to be paid as a visible passthrough on the invoice, or can we incorporate a reseller netback (gross->net) and route funds off-platform?
- If passthrough is required, what target netback (percent) should we size to for your channel partners?
- Are there procurement constraints on list price visibility (i.e., must list and private offer price be identical in the marketplace listing)?

I cc'd AWS marketplace so they can confirm the technicalities for pass-through vs rebate handling in the private offer flow. Attaching a draft offer and a short pricing scenarios workbook — will update once we lock the channel treatment.

Next step: if you can confirm preferred margin handling by EOD tomorrow we’ll produce the revised private offer document for legal and AWS review.

Hi Hannah,

Thanks — good summary. A few clarifications from procurement:
- We prefer visible passthrough on the invoice where possible; our finance team needs to see partner fees separately for compliance and cost allocation.
- Target netback for our strategic partners is typically 10–15% depending on partner role (reseller vs systems integrator). For an initial pass, assume 12% netback.
- We do not require list and private offer prices to be identical, but any large deltas require a short note for our auditors.

Also: can Redwood provide an example invoice path (how the charge appears on our bill, and how partner uplift is represented)? AWS marketplace confirmation copied in would be helpful.

Hannah / team — see quick scenarios below. I kept the math conservative to protect Redwood net and included a fallback clause.

Scenario A — Reserved + Metered (example monthly basis):
- Customer gross list price (visible on AWS listing): $120,000/mo (committed capacity)
- Partner visible fee line (12% netback): $14,400/mo
- Redwood net before taxes: $105,600/mo
- Overage: metered at $0.12/token; partner fee applied pro-rata to base, not to metered overage (recommended to avoid complexity).

Scenario B — Pure Metered Private Offer:
- Customer gross effective price (for invoice aggregation): varies by consumption; assume $100k in month one
- Partner visible fee (12% netback): $12,000
- Redwood net: $88,000
- Suggest applying partner fee as an on-invoice line item named 'Partner Fee (Atlas resellers)' so finance sees passthrough.

Recommendations / clauses:
- Keep partner fee as a visible passthrough on the AWS invoice. Redwood will treat this as a pass-through liability and remit to partner per settlement schedule.
- Fallback: if AWS cannot render a visible partner line, include a short fallback clause: 'If marketplace constraints prevent direct passthrough display, Redwood will provide monthly partner settlement statements and separate invoice/crediting to Atlas.'
- Legal language suggestion (one-liner): 'Customer acknowledges that a partner fee will be shown as a separate line item on the marketplace invoice; Redwood will remit partner fees to the designated partner in accordance with the private offer and settlement terms.'

I ran the numbers in the attached workbook (pricing-scenarios.xlsx). Connor — can you confirm if there are any settlement timing constraints from finance (Net 30 vs AWS's publisher payout windows)?

-ben
